raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`_score_kernel` and `_combine_kernel` in `srt/layers/attn_residual.py` read the attention-residual bank `[T, NB, H]` at `bank_ptr + pid_t * stride_bm`. `pid_t = tl.program_id(0)` is int32 and so is the product. With Kimi-K3's `NB = 8`, `H = 7168`, `stride_bm = 57,344`, so the offset passes 2^31 − 1 at `pid_t = 37,450`: any call with **≥ 37,451 tokens** reads at a negative offset and dies with `an illegal memory access was encountered`. The error is reported asynchronously, usually at a later, unrelated launch.

Where this path runs:
- **SM100+ (Blackwell):** the main aggregation uses the int64-safe TMA kernel, but `_mix_fused` still runs for the DSpark aux-hidden capture (`aggregate_stream`). So a DSpark prefill pass with more than 37,450 tokens (e.g. `--chunked-prefill-size` ≥ 40k) crashes.
- **GPUs without the TMA path:** `_mix_fused` is the main aggregation of every layer.
- `attn_res_hip.py`'s `_agg_kernel` has the same `t * stride_bm` pattern.

## Modifications

- Cast the token program id to int64 in `_score_kernel`, `_combine_kernel` (`attn_residual.py`) and `_agg_kernel` (`attn_res_hip.py`). Only addressing changes.
- New GPU test `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_attn_res_mix_large_tokens.py`: runs `_mix_fused` at T = 37,451 and checks the tail rows bitwise against a run on the tail alone (rows are independent).

## Accuracy Tests

Only addressing changes. Outputs are bitwise identical to the current kernels at T = 16 / 512 / 8,192 / 32,768 (1×GB300).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`_mix_fused` latency, NB = 8, H = 7168, nvb = 7, 1×GB300 (mean of 2 runs per arm):

| T | main (µs) | this PR (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 58.4 | 56.0 |
| 512 | 60.0 | 57.3 |
| 8,192 | 606.6 | 608.7 (+0.3%) |
| 32,768 | 2,388.7 | 2,397.6 (+0.4%) |

New test on 1×GB300: passes with this PR. On main it fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered`.

Tested on v0.5.21 (the `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130` image; main needs sglang-kernel ≥ 0.4.9). The kernels are unchanged between v0.5.21 and main. The HIP kernel change was not run on ROCm.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] GPU regression test added (`base-b-kernel-unit`, `1-gpu-large`).
- [x] No documentation change needed.
- [x] Accuracy and speed results above.

detail.title: [Fix] attn_residual: int64 program ids in the score/combine kernels (int32 overflow at 37,451 tokens)

files.patch:
@@ -83,7 +83,7 @@ def _agg_kernel(
     Taking the global max before exponentiating makes this bit-comparable to
     the 2-kernel pipeline rather than to the SM100 kernel.
     """
-    t = tl.program_id(0)
+    t = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)  # t * stride_bm overflows int32
     offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)
     mask = offs < H

@@ -133,7 +133,7 @@ def _score_kernel(
     BLOCK_H: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     """One CTA per (token, row): scan H, output one scalar score."""
-    pid_t = tl.program_id(0)
+    pid_t = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)  # pid_t * stride_bm overflows int32
     j = tl.program_id(1)
     if j > NVB:
         return
@@ -174,7 +174,7 @@ def _combine_kernel(
     Softmax is redundantly computed by each H-chunk CTA (≤16 elements, trivial).
     This gives full H-parallelism: 7 CTAs for H=7168/1024.
     """
-    pid_t = tl.program_id(0)
+    pid_t = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)  # pid_t * stride_bm overflows int32
     pid_h = tl.program_id(1)
     h0 = pid_h * BLOCK_H

@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+"""The attention-residual score/combine kernels index the [T, 8, 7168] bank with
+pid_t * stride_bm, which overflows int32 at 37,451 rows."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attn_residual import _mix_fused
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+_H, _NB, _NVB = 7168, 8, 7
+_T = 2**31 // (_NB * _H) + 2  # 37,451: the first row count whose offset overflows
+
+
+class TestAttnResMixLargeTokens(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+            raise unittest.SkipTest("CUDA is not available")
+
+    def test_rows_past_int32_offset(self):
+        g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+        prefix = torch.randn(_T, _H, generator=g, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+        bank = torch.randn(_T, _NB, _H, generator=g, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+        proj = SimpleNamespace(weight=torch.randn(1, _H, device="cuda") * _H**-0.5)
+        norm = SimpleNamespace(
+            weight=1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(_H, device="cuda"), variance_epsilon=1e-6
+        )
+
+        out = _mix_fused(prefix, bank, _NVB, proj, norm)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+        # Rows are independent, so the tail must match a run on the tail alone,
+        # whose offsets fit in int32.
+        n = 4096
+        tail = _mix_fused(prefix[-n:], bank[-n:], _NVB, proj, norm)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(out).all())
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out[-n:], tail))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
